name: represents-unused
body: I6 person/user linkage audit. State: 0 `represents` edges exist. The three solution.person.* nodes link to the system via `uses` (deck-author, template-author and maintainer -> solution.system.kalide); the two requirements.user.* nodes link to requirements via `contains`. What is missing relative to a literal reading of I6: there is no User->Entity or Entity->Person `represents` chain, and no person<->user pairing beyond the shared names deck-author and template-author (the maintainer is a stakeholder, not a user). Reason: the domain tier models no actor/individual entity (entities are deck, slide, section, template, theme, template-library, release and the deck-changed/deck-rebuilt events), and the `represents` schema is User->Entity plus Entity->Person, so the chain cannot be expressed without first modelling an actor entity. The model therefore links the tiers implicitly by name and by person->system `uses`. Options: (a) leave as-is — no represents, implicit name mapping (current intent); (b) add domain actor entities (e.g. a deck-author entity, a template-author entity) and then represents user->entity plus entity->person; (c) if the binary also permits a direct User->Person represents, add the two same-name edges. No edge added — needs the human gate [with user].
